title: Clamp a bar in a lathe's three-jaw chuck at a set stick-out and bring the turning tool up to its end face
instruction: Clamp the aluminium bar in the lathe chuck with 55 to 65 mm sticking out of the jaws, then move the tool so its tip is 1 to 3 mm from the end of the bar and 0 to 3 mm outside its diameter, without touching the bar.
context: Loading stock and bringing the tool up before the first cut is how every lathe job starts, so it affects millions of machinists and lathe operators, who do it many times a shift. The stick-out decides whether the part can be turned to length without chatter. A tool crashed into the stock or a loose chuck is how lathe accidents start.
setup: Distances from the robot: x away from the arm bases, y to the left (+) or right (-), heights above the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and -0.305 m (right). Bench lathe (fixed to the table, powered off, spindle locked): spindle axis along y at x 0.300, 60 mm up. Bed: cast iron, 70 mm wide (x 0.265 to 0.335), 12 mm tall, from y -0.250 to +0.230. Headstock on the left: a block 100 mm wide (x 0.250 to 0.350), from y 0.112 to 0.230, 95 mm tall, with a 36 mm square spindle bore that is closed 100 mm behind the jaw faces (y 0.160). Chuck: steel three-jaw chuck 80 mm in diameter and 40 mm deep (y 0.072 to 0.112), 32 mm bore, face towards the right (-y). Three steel jaws, 25 mm long along the axis (front faces at y 0.060), 10 mm wide, 12 mm deep: one straight below the axis, the others 30 deg above horizontal on either side; open at the start, their inner faces 15 mm from the axis (30 mm apart). Chuck key (steel), in a socket on top of the chuck at y 0.095: an 8 mm shaft 28 mm tall with a T-handle 60 x 10 x 10 mm on top (centre 133 mm up), the handle turned 29 deg anticlockwise from the x axis (seen from above). Turning the key clockwise (seen from above) closes the jaws together, 11 mm over 92 deg; it stays where it is left. Carriage (steel): a saddle 180 mm (x 0.165 to 0.345) by 95 mm (y -0.165 to -0.070), its top 26 mm up, riding on the bed along y; a black grab knob 12 mm in diameter stands on it at (0.180, -0.090), its top 61 mm up. Cross-slide (steel) on the carriage, 95 mm (x 0.170 to 0.265) by 40 mm (y -0.150 to -0.110), 10 mm thick, moving along x; on it a tool post 24 x 18 x 34 mm and a square 8 mm high-speed-steel tool bit 40 mm long pointing towards the axis (+x), its tip (the bit's corner nearest the chuck and the axis) at (0.255, -0.120), 60 mm up (spindle height); a black grab knob 12 mm in diameter at (0.180, -0.140), its top 70 mm up. Each slide stays where it is left; the carriage travels up to 170 mm towards the chuck, the cross-slide up to 50 mm towards the axis. Bar (loose): 6061 aluminium, 20 mm in diameter, 140 mm long, 119 g, lying along y, centre at (0.220, -0.290), in a cradle of two pine rails (fixed), each 10 mm wide, 5 mm tall and 150 mm long, 64 mm apart inside, either side of the bar.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial. Stick-out: from the jaws' front faces to the bar's free end, along the spindle axis. Clamped: all three jaws on the bar (each within 0.7 mm of its surface) and tightened, each pressing on it with at least 4 N (the key turned 11 deg or more past the point where the jaws first touch the bar), with the bar's axis within 1 mm of the spindle axis at the jaw faces and within 1 deg of it. Tool lined up: the tool tip 1 to 3 mm from the bar's end face along the axis, and 0 to 3 mm outside the bar's diameter (11 to 13 mm from the bar's axis). Touched: the tool came within 0.3 mm of the bar at any time in the trial. Score 0: the bar not clamped (loose, held by the robot, in the open jaws, or not in the chuck). 0.25: clamped, stick-out outside 55 to 65 mm. 0.5: clamped with 55 to 65 mm of stick-out, but the tool not lined up or it touched the bar. 1.0: clamped with 55 to 65 mm of stick-out and the tool lined up, never having touched the bar. The trial also ends early, at 1.0, once that has held for 2 s.
reset_notes: Turn the key anticlockwise to its start (handle 29 deg anticlockwise from x; the jaws open to 30 mm), take the bar out and lay it back in its cradle, and wind the carriage and cross-slide back to their start (tool tip at (0.255, -0.120)).
fidelity: Rigid primitives in PhysX at true size; the chuck body is a 12-sided ring, and the round bar a 12-sided prism (within 0.35 mm of round), which lets the gripper pads and jaws bear on it face to face. The scroll is simplified: the three jaws are geared together and sprung (3,000 N/m each) towards the position the key sets, and the key does not stall when the jaws meet the bar (a real key stops; here the grip goes on rising, to 12 N a jaw at the demo's 75 deg turn). The lathe's surfaces have a friction of 0.15, so the jaws slide an off-centre bar to the middle. The carriage and cross-slide handwheels are replaced by grab knobs on damped slides that stay where they are left. The lathe is off and the spindle locked; nothing is cut.
